newsitem.title: TUNISIA: Tunisia plans opening forex to resident banks.
newsitem.headline: Tunisia plans opening forex to resident banks.

text.p: Tunisia's Central Bank governor on Saturday said there were plans to allow resident banks to have foreign exchange operations with foreign banks, expanding the domestic day-to-day interbank market established since 1994.
"We plan a new step in the foreign exchange activities," Mohamed Beji Hamda told the annual congress of Tunisian forex dealers.

"The opening up of banks to the international environment would prepare them to face foreign competition and improve their expertise in matters of international exchange and treasury and in progressively taking in charge the management of forex risk," he added.
The governor did not set a date for the opening, but bankers told Reuters it was expected by mid-1997.

"This new step in the financial liberalisation will contribute to the decompartmentalisation between the various money markets and toward the progressive establishement of an harmonious, efficient and global capital market," Hamda said.
Transactions handled on the interbank market throughout 1995 amounted to 6.5 billion dinars (6.5 billion), Central bank sources said.

The share of interbank transactions, in which the US dollar and the French franc accounted for two-thirds, was nearly 80 percent in total exchange operations. The remaining 20 percent were handled by the Central Bank for the state's operations.

"The market will open up and will allow us to deal with the (world's) professional operators and therefore will improve our management of risks and enable us to meet the firms needs," Houssein Mouelhi, head of Amen Bank forex department told Reuters commenting on Hamda's statement.
Currently only Tunis-based off shore banks are allowed to have forex operations with foreign banks.
The Central Bank governor warned the Tunisian banks that they must reform themselves to be able to assume the charge of tyhe forex risk management.
"In this perspective, the banks are called to take all the safety measures needed by the management of currency operations...," he said.
